trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether 2026 fed funds futures (SOFR strip) and the 2yr yield moved in the same direction as the implied cut probability; if not, treat as noise.
time_plan.1h: Compare TLT intraday move vs Fed-speak headlines or data releases; determine if market lagged or led.
time_plan.2h: Re-check whether the cut-count probability shift persisted or reverted; confirm 10yr yield direction.
time_plan.6h: Assess whether any FOMC-relevant catalyst (data, speaker) explains the move publicly.
time_plan.12h: Evaluate total TLT move vs expectation; log whether the prediction-market signal had any lead over Treasuries.

predictions.reasoning: This market tracks the number of 25bp Fed cuts in 2026, a direct proxy for market-implied Fed easing. A sharp rise in the implied probability of cuts signals more dovish expectations, which pushes bond yields down and long-duration Treasury prices (TLT) up. However, the causality is usually the reverse: rate-cut odds move BECAUSE of macro data (CPI, NFP, Fed speak) that already move Treasuries first. This prediction market is unlikely to lead the bond tape, and a marginal probability shift in one specific cut-count bucket maps to only a few basis points of TLT movement over 12h — far below the 700bps tradable threshold.

predictions.reasoning: More expected Fed cuts narrow rate differentials and typically weaken the dollar, so a rising cut-probability would nudge UUP down. But the dollar responds to global relative rates, risk sentiment, and other central banks, so a single-bucket US cut-count probability is a weak and noisy proxy. Expected 12h magnitude is tiny (~10-20bps), well below the 700bps tradable bar, and the market almost certainly reacts to the same public data rather than leading it.

evidence_used: Market question tracks the count of 25bp Fed cuts in 2026, a direct read on Fed easing expectations
Rate-cut expectations map mechanically to Treasury yields (inverse to TLT) and to the US dollar
Standard macro linkage: more cuts => lower yields, higher bond prices, weaker USD
uncertainty_notes: Causality typically runs from public macro data to both rate-cut odds and asset prices, so this market likely lags rather than leads
A marginal shift in one specific cut-count bucket carries little information vs the full easing distribution
The mislabeled 'military_conflict' topic suggests metadata noise; treat category as unreliable
No actual probability move is given here, so direction is conditional on an assumed dovish shift

llm_justification.summary: This is a US monetary-policy market whose implied probability tracks expected Fed easing in 2026. A dovish shift (higher odds of cuts) maps to higher long-Treasury prices (TLT) and a weaker dollar (UUP). But these are weak, lagging proxies: the market almost certainly reacts to the same public CPI/NFP/Fed-speak that already move rates, and the mechanical 12h impact is only tens of basis points — far below the 700bps tradable threshold. Direction is plausible but magnitude and lead-time are low, so this is non-tradable, low-confidence research signal.
key_assumptions: A relevant move in the market is a dovish shift raising cut probability
Standard rate-transmission linkages hold over the 12h window
Liquidity and normal market conditions (no shock)
failure_modes: The rate-cut odds move because of already-public data, giving no informational lead over TLT/UUP
A hawkish/less-cuts shift would reverse both predicted directions
Single-bucket cut-count is a weak proxy for the full easing path; the yield curve may move only at the front end
Dollar move dominated by foreign central bank or risk-sentiment factors unrelated to Fed cuts
Expected magnitude is far below 700bps, so any apparent signal is likely noise
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
